Amazing food and dining!
Oct 2026 • Couples
What a gem! We wanted to get away from Hoi An Old town and the standard Vietnamese fare. Found Mua and are so glad we did. The tasting menu had a wide variety of new takes on locally-grown food and preparation. Greens and salad were super-fresh. Meats were raised and caught nearby.

Speaking of nearby, this is a bit out of the way - in Tra Que, about a 15-minute taxi from Old Town - so you need to plan to get there.

The tasting menu was wonderful. While a couple of the 15(!) courses fell a tad flat, most were outstanding. The variety of ingredients, textures, temperatures, presentations, and tastes kept both our attention and our palettes engaged. The alcohol pairing melded well with the courses, especially the sake flight.

The ambience was comfortable, quiet, and bohemian. The pouring rain while we were there added to the coziness. Each table has its own floor lamp made of a natural tree branch. The tableware was varied and elegant. Chairs were comfortable and conducive to lingering over each course.

After the first few courses of the tasting menu, I was worried that I might end up hungry after the meal but I was wrong. It was the perfect amount of food. I was pleasantly sated but not too full.

The staff were fun. Their enthusiasm for the ingredients and mission was evident. One waiter went above and beyond to help get us a taxi in the pouring rain through 6-inch deep water - giving us a spontaneous tour of their farm along the way.

Overall the best meal we've had in Vietnam, and an absolutely delicious diversion from the menu of "local specialties" served by most restaurants. It wasn't cheap compared to most local restaurants. It cost us just shy of 3,000,000 VND for two people (tasting menu) plus a shared alcohol pairing. That's about $120 USD, which is a quarter the price a 15-course tasting menu of this caliber would cost in the US. Overall a great value if you seek out really good food in a nice dining atmosphere.

Fantastic meal at Mua. We were dragged along by friends and had no idea where we were going. 
We had already provided our allergies and preferences in advance, and on site it turned out that the dinner is a 15-course menu served in 5 courses. Everything we had indicated was taken into account. Very nice and very tasty.

Mua is an exceptional dining experience
Dec 2025 • Friends
I have travelled to Hoi An on many occasions, but this was my first experience at Mua, and what an experience it was. The location is spectacular, and takes you right into the heart of the natural beauty of the Hoi An Countryside. 
Uyen and her talented team have taken Vietnamese cuisine, already some of the best in the world and elevated to an exceptional level.
The 14-course tasting menu, using locally grown and seasonal produce, takes you on an incredible culinary journey from start to finish. Every course is thoughtful, well presented, and tastes incredible, and showcases Vietnamese cuisine at the very highest level
To complement the food, Uyen has also carefully selected wine pairings for each course, and they match perfectly, enhancing every dish and making the overall experience even more memorable.
This is without doubt one of the best dining experiences I have had in Vietnam, I cannot recommend Mua highly enough, it is an absolute must visit for anyone travelling to Hoi An, especially if you are a true food lover

A gastro design in Hoi an
Sep 2024 • Couples
On arrival beautiful welcome, very clean place, space between tables that gives a very pleasant intimate side...

We are presented with the concept, we take the time to tell us the taste journey that the chef proposes...
Between revisited local recipes and fusion discoveries. 
The idea of a two formula menu to choose from, we opted for the reduced formula, 8 courses...
This comes in small portions.

We received the 4 starters at the same time, maybe it would have been more accurate to space these dishes so we could taste them between texture, taste and presentation...

We had fun for 3 of them, but the oyster shell with its "squid/fruit tartare genre" with this viscous sauce was very surprising in both senses of the word.
As a dish the duck very thin, and the rolls may be a little too thick for chewing, but tasty.
2 delicious desserts..

For us Europeans, very affordable gastronomy about 80 euros for two people nothing to say..

Staff with little care, available, smiling a real pleasure

Outstanding food in a gorgeous informal setting
Apr 2024 • Couples
An absolutely outstanding place. 

We’ve eaten very well indeed throughout Vietnam but this place is exceptional. The evening tasting menu offers an astonishing array of flavours, with every dish beautifully presented and its components fully explained by the lovely staff. 

It’s tucked away down a lane surrounded by organic farmland (which supplies much of the restaurant’s ingredients), on an island fifteen minutes by taxi from Hoi An. 

It’s fine dining indeed but in a very relaxed and informal setting, with attentive but charmingly unfussy staff. 

We were so bowled over by last night’s dinner that we’re going back again today for lunch. 

It’s expensive for Vietnam but still eminently affordable by U.K. standards. We had 15 small dishes, aperitifs (including the restaurant’s own take on Japanese sake), three glasses of wine each, and a digestif. The bill was £85. 

We were blown away.

Vietnamese fusion at its best
Feb 2020 • Couples
What do you get when you combine Vietnamese flavours with french technique and add a dash of personality to it ? Answer : Mùa - which means "seasons". This charming venue, started by ex-Boston chef Tru Lang, is located near the rice paddies, away from the noise of old town. Most ingredients are sourced from a garden 2 minutes away as well as other regions of Vietnam. What we call farm-to-table, locals call...food, explains Chef Tru. His unique take on the fusion genre which celebrates fresh, local ingredients had us nodding our heads after every bite. As an extra twist, my wife is on a FODMAP diet - no onions, garlic, mushrooms amongst other restrictions - which the chef was able to accommodate without breaking a sweat.

On to the food. Here's the breakdown of our lunch.

Amuse-bouche : Bánh tét chuối with caviar. Crunchy, salty, sour in just the right way. I could eat this all day.

Appetizer : Spring roll with herbs from Trà quế gardens and pumpkin served with peanut sauce. A mosaic of the neighbouring garden's best herbs layered around pumpkin. So fresh and so clean.

Entrée : Hand cut bánh canh noodles with smoked eggplant, shrimp butter served with poached egg on top and Tomme from mộc châu on the side. Bursting with umami and seafood flavors.
Served with a glass of Đà Lạt red wine and crushed mulberries to wash down all that goodness.

Dessert : Passion fruit crème brûlée with mango and passion fruit, Đà Lạt yogurt sprinkled with fresh bee pollen. Henceforth "the forbidden dessert", as I forbid the chef from removing this item from the menu. Why have I never tasted this combination before ?

Digestif : Kavalan Solist Oloroso Sherry Single Cask. In whiskey buff parlance : yum. What a perfect ending to this meal.

I wish our stay in Hoi An had been longer so I could have dinner at Mùa. If I was living in town, I would be eating here all the time. Do yourself a favour, grab a bike, head out to the rice paddies and keep going, straight to Mùa.

This meal set the bar for the rest of our 3-week stay in Vietnam. I noticed after the fact that this was a vegetarian lunch, but the meat-lover in me was somehow satisfied. Thank you Chef Tru for an unforgettable experience.
